mods.name: Inhabited (local)
mods.author: mandrake
mods.description:
Somebody lives here.

RimWorld's world map is a set of props: a settlement is a name and a loot table, a visitor is a timer. Inhabited gives places a persistent cast of real pawns who live there, and lets the world remember what the player did to them.

Four nouns:
- PLACE — a structure on a tile, from the tile-mutator / landmark layer.
- CAST — the people who belong to it. A persistent roster of real Pawn objects, never a spawn list.
- ROUTE — what the cast does across a day.
- FATE — what, if anything, could end them. The default is nothing: they live here.

The roster is held in a WorldObject as a ThingOwner<Pawn>, the same container Caravan uses, so names, skills, relationships, scars and memories survive map destruction with no serialisation of our own. The survivors return to the roster when the player leaves; the dead are simply forgotten. Pawns the player sells into a cast stay there and remember it.

People who lose their place enter a per-faction pool of the placeless, and any cast being instantiated draws from that pool before generating anyone new — so the beggars at the player's gate may be the crew whose refinery they burned.

There is no morality system here and there must never be one. The consequence is delivered entirely by RimWorld's existing name, backstory and memory systems, plus the player's own recognition.

NPCs do not farm — three shipped walls make it impossible — so a place's sustenance is present rather than produced: a mess, a paste vat, a granary, a herd. It is visible, stealable and destroyable, and burning it makes the cast leave rather than starve.

mods.name: Planet Preset Prime (local)
mods.author: mandrake
mods.description:
A development ergonomics fix, not player-facing content. Players never see the world-creation page - they receive a savegame holding the frozen world - but WE re-create test worlds constantly, and the page forgets its settings every single time.

RimWorld persists nothing about the planet preset. Page_CreateWorldParams.Reset() re-chooses planetCoverage from a hardcoded default on every open, and My Little Planet's subdivision count is likewise re-chosen. Config/Prefs.xml has 63 keys and not one of them mentions planet, coverage, subcount or seed; My Little Planet writes no mod config at all.

Ash'karr is a 21,872-tile planet, which is coverage 1.0 at subcount 7. Open the page at the defaults instead and you get 119,904 tiles - and world/ASHKARR_WORLDMAP_tiles.csv addresses 0..21871, so every one of those rows then points at different ground. A paint run reports success while writing a scrambled planet. That is the failure this exists to prevent.

One Harmony postfix on Page_CreateWorldParams.Reset() sets both values. Reset() is the method that actually assigns them and it runs exactly once, behind PreOpen's initialized flag.

It PRIMES, it does not LOCK. The fields stay public and settable, so dragging a slider still overrides it.

This is only half the defence and the other half is deliberately kept: src/RimMandrake/Utils/w9_run.py holds EXPECT_TILES = 21872 and refuses to import when the live world disagrees. The mod stops the mistake being made; the guard stops it being acted on.

mods.name: Wrecked Machines
mods.author: Mandrake
mods.description:
Ancient wreckage.

Ancient machines do not fail politely. They are found where they died — split open, scavenged, corroded, half-buried in their own slag — and some of them are still, faintly, working. Ancient technology is robust: it does not stop, it sags. A wrecked power cell still trickles current. Bring one home, study it, and build it back up one grade at a time.

Every treated machine sits on one ladder of grades:

  WRECKED      Dead, or nearly. Inert — except that a wrecked power source
               still trickles a faint current.
  KLUDGED      Works, badly, visibly bodged. About a fifth of the original.
  REFURBISHED  The ceiling you normally reach: three-quarters of the original,
               and still visibly a kludge. Needs scarce ancient components.
  ORIGINAL     The machine as it was built. Off by default — a Mod Setting
               allows full restoration.

Each grade is built over the one below it. Studying the wreck itself is how you
learn to restore it (with Research Reinvented, the wreck is the research
subject). Mobile machines are on the ladder too: salvaged power cells and
psychic emanators can be carried off and installed wherever they are needed.

Advancing a grade costs materials, tools and earned knowledge, never a research
grind alone. Every ratio is tunable in Mod Settings.

This mod ships its own art for all three states and does not replace or alter
any other mod's buildings. The donor mod's original Automated Smelter ThingDef
is left completely untouched — its stats, comps and recipes are unchanged, and
our smelter grades still run its own processes — but it no longer
appears in the Architect build menu, so a player cannot build a fresh one
alongside our grades. Vanilla's own hand-run electric smelter is untouched
and unrelated.

mods.name: RimMandrake: FlowWorks
mods.author: Mandrake
mods.description:
Dig a channel, let a fluid flow into it: a species- and
biome-agnostic engine for canals that carry water, ooze, slime, oil, tar or
fuel from a source into the terrain a colonist chooses.

Depth is the primitive. Every excavated cell carries two small integers — D,
how far below the surface it was dug (shallow, mid, deep, SUPERDEEP), and F,
how much liquid is in it — and everything else is a function of those two on
one cell: what it costs to cross, how much it holds, and which liquid surface
is drawn. We dig down; we never build up. There is no elevation model, no
height advantage, and no fluid simulation: liquid levels itself out on a
pulse, by sorting the deepest cells first and letting a full one overflow
into whatever has room.

A natural liquid body IS a source — deep terrain that is already full, which
is why it spills into a shallower channel dug at its edge. Liquid stays in
what has been excavated.

Shipped: the depth/fill grid and its pulse engine
(`RM_MapComponent_Excavation`), a dig designator that deepens a cell each
time it is used, depth-derived movement cost, a three-tier fill ladder on
vanilla's own edge-aware water ramps, and `FluidDef`s describing what a
source carries — water and tar for canals, plus the wider LiquidDef
registry (below) covering fifteen liquid types with their own terrain suites
and bottled forms. Bottles, buckets and barrels fill and wash at a
matching liquid's shore, and a buildable liquid tank holds a bulk stock of
one liquid at a time, filled and drained by the same containers.

A SUPERDEEP excavation is the trapping level and the only one: anything that
walks into one falls in and is held there whether the hole is dry or brimming,
and gets out only by climbing a ladder somebody built down there. Pull the
ladder and they stay. Depth touches shooting in exactly one way, and it is a
restriction rather than an advantage — whoever is in a superdeep hole can only
trade fire with whoever is standing right at its lip, both directions.

Burning liquids are built (a fuse creeps along tar or oil once vanilla fire
touches it) but not yet proven in a live game. Not yet built, and named so
nobody thinks they are missing: sluice gates and irrigation.

The engine writes the map's temporary terrain layer, which
is base-game machinery, and ships its own temporary terrains rather than
naming the Odyssey-only ones. Harmony is required.

MERGED IN 2026-09-16 (FLOWWORKS_BUILD_PROGRAM_1 Phase 1) — one mod now owns
the whole liquid domain, per the owner's ruling that depth is the single
primitive underneath all of it:

PITS. A pit is any canal cell dug down to superdeep — there is no pit
building. Whoever walks, is pushed or jumps in takes a fall and, if the pit is
as wide as they are, cannot climb out until a ladder stands in their cell.
They stay on the map, on the pit floor.

WATER EFFECTS (was mandrake.rm.manywaters). The generic water-effects
engine: animated river-steam ambience off a biome's own opt-in extension,
RM_DeepSand (impassable, fishable sand built the way vanilla deep water is),

  breach walls, hole thin roofs and leave rubble as they walk, struggle under
  overhead mountain, butcher for a curved yield, and the largest leave a corpse

THE SOAK. Ground becomes SOAKED when qualifying fresh water arrives in quantity, and dries back over hours to a day.   - Slime: the ring turns the ground to slime.
  - Rupture (contaminated plants): a gas cloud, spawned things, sprouts, and mutations for anyone in the cloud without a full vacuum seal.
  - Flush (giant trees): it swells inside and survives, silently.

mods.author: Mandrake
mods.description:
STAGED_LORE_BUILD_1 — descriptions that change as a story is learned.

A def's description, settle warning or label is rewritten to match how far a campaign's reveal ladder has advanced, so a place can read as an inexplicable wasteland until the player earns the truth and then read as what it is. The engine only; no lore text lives here.

HOW: every display surface that matters reads a def FIELD at draw time (the world tile inspector reads BiomeDef.description directly, Thing.DescriptionFlavor is a virtual with no backing store, the settle confirmation re-reads BiomeDef.settleWarning every time), so a field write shows on the next frame and no Harmony patch is needed. Ludeon ships the same idea in the base game: Building_VoidMonolith stages its description by campaign level.

THE TWO TRAPS IT HANDLES: (1) ThingDef.descriptionDetailedCached and HediffDef.descriptionCached are private memoized fields that NO engine path ever clears, so trade/transfer rows, storage filters and hediff tooltips would keep serving the previous stage's text for the rest of the session — this mod nulls both by reflection on every apply. (2) Defs are process-global and are not reloaded between savegames, so a stage-5 colony's text would still be on the def when a stage-0 save loads — every apply resets to the shipped baseline first and then applies the current stage from scratch.

WHAT SHIPS: GameComponent_LoreStage (scribes a per-ladder stage into the .rws, applies on FinalizeInit — which covers both a new game and every load) and RM_LoreStageTableDef, the data-side ladder table that content mods provide. Ladders advance independently. Dev-mode debug actions under "Lore stages" set any ladder's rung and dump what every staged field currently holds.

Loads and does nothing at all when no RM_LoreStageTableDef is present.

mods.description:
OASIS_MAKER_BUILD_1 (owner ruling, 2026-09-24, verbatim: "machines that
create oases slowly when placed near shaded terrain near rocks. Placement is
key. We should guide it with green red area selections... Makes obtaining the
ancient machines a treasure type."). Spec: design/RimMandrake/oasis_maker_machines_spec.md.

A treasure-class ancient building (`RM_OasisMaker`, minifiable) that, once
placed on cold shaded stone, wakes after a short attuning window and then
grows an oasis around itself ring by ring, on its own clock — no power, no
fuel, no colonist labor. Terrain climbs a stepwise natural ladder
(Sand/SoftSand -> Gravel -> Soil -> SoilRich at the margin; Soil -> Mud ->
Marsh -> WaterShallow at the innermost ring, forming a real, fishable,
stockable pool at the machine's heart) — never floors, never constructed
terrain, never existing water, never stone. Placement is guided by a live
green/red projected-footprint overlay that recomputes per ghost move, the
same shape as vanilla's `PlaceWorker_WatermillGenerator`: red means the
hard floor (shaded cells + standing rock nearby) is not met and the machine
refuses to place; green shows the oasis the current spot would actually
grow, sized and paced by how good the spot is. Interrupting it (uninstall,
destruction, losing its shade/rock) freezes growth forever — everything
already converted stays; nothing this mod does ever reverses a cell.

**Acquisition (RULED, owner typed, 2026-09-24): "They are sold but very
expensive. Same tech as moisture farming itself. You can start a colony with
some of those. And priced accordingly."** Not craftable in v1 — the machine
is tagged for exotic-goods trader stock (`ExoticMisc`, treasure-class market
value) and is an ordinary minifiable buildable, so it is legal starting gear
in the scenario editor exactly like any other tradeable minified building.
Quest obtain/sabotage hooks are deferred to the quest-design passes per the
spec; this mod ships the mechanism only.

Tier: RimMandrake (`RM_`) — works on any map with shade and rock, not tied
to any one biome. Feature-gated: Mod Settings carries a master on/off plus
every rate and floor number named in the spec (shade/rock floor, attuning
length, base ring time, per-ring growth factor, radius cap band).

**Pool integration**: a newly grown `WaterShallow` cell fires the public
`RimMandrake.OasisMaker.RM_OasisPoolIntegration.PoolCellCreated` event
(map, cell, source="RM_OasisMaker") so a grown oasis registers with the
Stocked Pool kit's bookkeeping (`STOCKED_POOL_BUILD_1`,
`RM_MapComponent_PoolStock`) exactly like a natural pool once that kit
subscribes — see this mod's own rimflow item for the exact contract, since
that component did not exist yet when this mod was built.

**Art**: the spec's own build-size table lists the comb-silhouette sprite
pass as its own S-sized line item separate from this mechanism sitting
(alongside the deferred quest weaves) — this build ships with a placeholder
texture pending that pass, tracked in the same item.

mods.name: RimMandrake: Solar Mirrors
mods.author: mandrake
mods.description:
Mirrors that move sunlight. SOLAR_MIRRORS_MOD_DESIGN_1 (design/RimMandrake/solar_mirrors_mod_design_2026-10-04.md).

A mirror throws a patch of sun onto a cell you pick. In that patch the shade is gone: it is hot, animals that hide from the sun route around it, and plants get more light where the sky is dim. Light reflects best back toward the sun's side and worst straight away from it. Walls, rock, closed doors and roofs stop a beam. A mirror standing in shadow throws nothing, unless another mirror lights it, so mirrors can be chained.

Buildings:
  - Signal mirror (1x1, no research). Aimed by a colonist (a re-aim job).
  - Static mirror (2x2, any metal; silver and gold reflect best). Aimed by a colonist. It does not track the sun, so where the sun moves its patch of light slowly sweeps.
  - Heliostat (3x3, powered). Aimed instantly and holds its target as the sun moves. Without power it freezes where it is and becomes a static mirror.
  - Sun-stone (1x1). Reads lit or unlit.
  - Solar furnace. Smelts with no fuel and no power, but only while concentrated light (two or more mirrors) falls on it. Indoors it warms its room.
  - Glazed aperture. A glass wall that mirror light passes through, on under the roof into the room behind it: a mirror-lit, mirror-warmed greenhouse.
  - Heliograph. By day a colonist at a sunlit signal mirror can flash a friendly settlement within reach and open talks with it.

Defence: hostile people standing in a beam slowly go glare-blind and shoot worse, unless goggles or a gene protect them.
Heat: where several beams overlap the light is stronger than the sun, and it feels hotter there, never past the biome's limit.
Upkeep: sand, grit and ash storms dull mirrors in the open until a colonist cleans them.

Ancient mirror fields: on the Long Shade, where the sun never moves, a map can hold a field of seized ancient heliostats before a sealed vault. Free their bearings, turn each between its old brass pins, and light every sun-stone to open the vault. Every field is checked to be solvable before it is placed.

Every effect has its own switch in Mod Settings (with an "all off" button that leaves inert decorative buildings). Mirror light is our own grid on top of the shade grid; it never adds a new kind of heat.

WARCASKET_SUIT_CLASS_1. A cross-cutting heavy survival-apparel class, generalized:
it names no biome, faction or campaign and is playable standalone on any generated RimWorld
planet. Owner ruling, 2026-09-28 (WASTELAND_BEDAZZLE_SITTING_1), verbatim: "Warcaskets REDEFINED
cross-cutting: very resistant to extreme temps + vacuum + toxins, an alternative to space suits
and ocean access, but very slow, bulky, prone to failure under compound threats — a primitive
tank around a person."

RM tier: nothing here knows what campaign or planet uses it. The Wasteland biome (and the frozen
Utinni campaign's own Wasteland instance) is this suit's primary use case — Junkers wear a
further-adjusted variant to extract fuel from ruined ground — but the suit class itself works
anywhere extreme temperature, vacuum or toxic-terrain protection matters: any DLC's space
exposure, any biome's toxic fallout, any modded ocean/brine shore.

Ships, all togglable in Mod Settings (defaults = shipped behavior, MOD_OPTIONS_RETROFIT_1
doctrine):

  1. RM_Warcasket — the base suit. Real stat coverage for all three hazard classes (extreme-temp
     Insulation_Cold/Insulation_Heat, vacuum via Odyssey's own VacuumResistance, toxin via
     Biotech's own ToxicEnvironmentResistance), a heavy MoveSpeed/WorkSpeedGlobal penalty ("very
     slow, bulky"), and a real compound-failure mechanic: RM_CompWarcasketIntegrity tracks how
     many hazard classes are simultaneously active against the wearer and rolls a genuine failure
     chance once two or more stack, damaging the suit and injuring the wearer with a tendable
     RM_WarcasketBreach hediff — not flavor text, an actual risk that scales with how compound the
     threat gets and how damaged the suit already is.
  2. RM_WarcasketJunker — a Junker-adjusted variant, and warcasket sarcophagi (wastes.md §7: "a
     dead Junker in an adjusted warcasket is a sealed salvage-within-salvage: suit, tools, and the
     half-extracted core still in its grips"). The suit seals onto its wearer at death, so ordinary
     stripping leaves it on the body; a colonist cracks it open from the corpse's right-click menu
     to recover the suit, the welded tooling and RM_HalfExtractedCore, a reactor core that doses
     everyone near it until it is locked in a cask bay.
  3. Terrain-survival wiring: RM_HazardousTerrainProtection (a summed apparel stat, same shape as
     TheRot's RM_SheenProtection) and RM_MapComponent_HazardousTerrainImmersion, a general
     hazard engine (not warcasket-specific — any apparel granting the stat helps, on any map) that
     applies RM_TerrainImmersionHazard to a pawn standing on deep/non-walkable water terrain
     without enough protection. Scoped deliberately to non-walkable ("must swim") water only —
     an ordinary shallow ford or marsh margin every biome already has pawns cross freely is never
     the hazard; only water nothing can simply walk across is. 🔴 This is TERRAIN survival only:
     it grants no dive verb, no MapPortal access, no sea-floor teleport of any kind. A sea FLOOR
     stays reachable only through a gravship's own RM_SeaDiveHatch — "the ship is the only way
     down and the only way back" (owner ruling, 2026-09-26). A warcasket lets its wearer stand
     safely at the edge or wade the shallows and margins of a hostile sea or brine pool; it never
     lets them dive to, or return from, the floor beneath one.

  4. RM_CaskBay — the lead-lined cask bay the sitting approved (BENCH slate item 7, owner "yrs"):
     "a shielded hardpoint that lets the ship haul the Throat's casks". A cask-only storage building
     that needs gravship substructure, so it flies with the ship; while shielding is on, stored
     toxic wastepacks never dissolve and stored cores give off no dose.
